Emily / team — quick technical primer to help procurement and infra set expectations before the session:

High-level estimates (based on the prompt set you uploaded and our modelling):
- Quantization: moving from FP16 to an 8-bit quant profile (per our validated Redwood-Opt-8 config) often yields ~2.0–2.8x reduction in model memory and ~10–18% per-token compute cost reduction in our runtime, depending on seq length and attention pattern. For your short chat prompts we conservatively estimate 12% per-token savings.
- KV/prefix cache: if queries reuse context (you indicated ~30% prompt overlap), a prefix/KV cache hitting at 30–45% can reduce generated token compute by an additional 20–35% (effective token spend reduction depends on hit distribution).
- Batching & concurrency: aim for 8–16 request batch windows with adaptive latency SLOs — this reduces per-token amortized compute cost meaningfully during peak.

Combined conservative estimate: 25–35% net reduction in billable tokens with the recommended config (quantized model + cache + batching). We’ll bring a notebook to the workshop showing per-prompt breakdown and sensitivity to hit rate.

Attachments: FastShip_AMS_MAWS_questionnaire.xlsx (filled-in infra notes), small notebook snapshot included in the Drive link.

Note on quality: access to a small eval set would let us run a quick quality regression check with the quantized variant during the workshop. If you want, we can slot that for the second half of the session.

—Aditya

Emily / Rajiv — appreciate the clarity on procurement targets. We want to be practical and give you an offer that reflects expected unit savings while keeping guardrails on technical risk. Proposed commercial options post-workshop: 

Option A — Pilot (low friction):
- 30-day pilot, $25k credit applied during pilot (covers compute + SE workshop hours)
- Pilot credits are fully applied to consumption if you sign a 12-month commit within 30 days of pilot end; otherwise the credits are non-refundable.

Option B — Efficiency Accelerator Pack (recommended for predictable savings):
- 12-month commit bands (monthly committed spend): Tier 1: $25k/mo (10% discount), Tier 2: $50k/mo (14% discount), Tier 3: $100k+/mo (18% discount)
- Included: pre-validated quantization profile, 4-hour on-site/remote ops runbook handoff, one-time KV cache warmup credits, and 2% monthly overage protection for burst events.
- If you provide a 3-month convertible pilot as runway for adoption we can offer a one-time conversion credit equal to 50% of pilot credits toward the commit (effectively improving the convert-to-commit economics).

Concession ask: we aren’t able to meet a straight 25% off list for a standard 12-month commit at our current pricing template, but for strategic customers we can consider an uplifted Tier 2 discount structure with an enterprise addendum (requires exec approval).

Next steps: we’ll run the workshop on Wed 10:00 PT. Post-workshop Aditya and SE team will drop the per-prompt savings notebook, and Ben/Sofia will share a one-page commercial term sheet and a DocuSign-ready proposal (docusign_proposal_2026-06-30.pdf). If procurement wants a CFO-friendly one-page TCO with upfront vs commit scenarios, we can prepare that within 48 hours.

If that sounds workable I’ll send the DocuSign link and the one-pager after the session.

Regards,
